submissions.findingTextShort: Human Scutellaria-root exposure measured wogonin-related analytes but is not an isolated-wogonin efficacy, safety, or dosing trial.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 12520178 studied ten healthy male volunteers receiving a commercial Scutellariae Radix/root-powder preparation and measured urinary wogonin, wogonoside and related flavone metabolites. This is parent-botanical human exposure/pharmacokinetic evidence; it does not establish isolated-wogonin efficacy, isolated-compound safety, or a consumer dose for wogonin.
submissions.populationContext: Ten healthy male volunteers receiving a commercial Scutellaria root preparation
submissions.usageContext: Parent-botanical human exposure and constituent pharmacokinetics
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Multiple root constituents and metabolites prevent causal attribution to isolated wogonin.

submissions.findingTextShort: Human fecal-microflora experiments support wogonoside-to-wogonin biotransformation but not therapeutic equivalence or human clinical efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 24412378 used simulated gastrointestinal digestion and human fecal microflora in vitro to characterize Scutellaria flavone metabolism toward aglycones including wogonin. The result supports a directional wogonoside-to-wogonin metabolic relationship; human-derived microbiota does not make this a human participant trial, and precursor/root outcomes cannot be transferred automatically to wogonin monotherapy.
submissions.populationContext: In-vitro gastrointestinal and human fecal-microflora system; no participant intervention
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Biotransformation establishes relationship, not therapeutic interchangeability or clinical effect magnitude.

submissions.findingTextShort: Wogonin CYP1A inhibition in human liver microsomes is an in-vitro interaction signal, not a quantified clinical drug interaction.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 30989924 identified potent CYP1A1/1A2 inhibition by wogonin using human liver microsomes and recombinant enzymes. This may justify an interaction-review flag, but human-derived microsomes are mechanistic evidence rather than a participant study and cannot establish patient-level interaction magnitude, contraindication thresholds, or clinical dosing adjustments.
submissions.populationContext: Human liver microsomes and recombinant enzyme systems; no human participants
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Clinical exposure, free concentrations, co-medications and in-vivo effect size remain unestablished.

submissions.findingTextShort: Transporter inhibition in HEK-cell assays is mechanistic screening evidence and cannot be promoted to a clinical interaction claim.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 24018852 used HEK-293 transporter-expression assays to evaluate wogonin effects on selected OAT, OATP and OCT transport systems. Human transporter proteins expressed in a cell system do not constitute a human intervention study; these findings may support mechanistic interaction hypotheses but not clinically quantified interaction risk or patient-specific contraindications.
submissions.populationContext: Engineered cell transporter assays; no human participants
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Translation from assay inhibition to clinically meaningful interaction requires proposition-compatible in-vivo evidence.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 systematic review of wogonin for sepsis remains preclinical and explicitly leaves clinical efficacy unestablished.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 41614556 systematically reviewed in-vivo and in-vitro preclinical wogonin evidence for sepsis and called for clinical trials. The recency and systematic-review design do not convert an animal/cell evidence base into human treatment evidence; the source instead reinforces the current researched clinical-evidence ceiling for isolated wogonin.
submissions.populationContext: Systematic review of preclinical in-vivo and in-vitro studies; no human treatment trials
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Preclinical consistency may motivate research but cannot establish human efficacy, safety, or dosing.
